issue_context.title: Suggest to Add  ssh-keygen -a (Trials) Option
issue_context.body:
### Summary

I am trying to achieve a best practise solution with ansible. I have found out that the -a Option from the underlying ssh-keygen is missing.


The -a Option would it allow to improve the security of the generated keys when creating users and their ssh-keys 
[SSH-Keygen](https://linux.die.net/man/1/ssh-keygen)

As the -a Option can help to protect against brute forcing.

The default is 100


### Issue Type

Feature Idea

### Component Name

user

### Additional Information

<!--- Paste example playbooks or commands between quotes below -->
```yaml (paste below)
- name: Create a 2048-bit SSH key for user jsmith in ~jsmith/.ssh/id_rsa
  ansible.builtin.user:
    name: jsmith
    generate_ssh_key: yes
    ssh_key_bits: 2048
    ssh_key_file: .ssh/id_rsa
    ssh_key_trials: 1000
    ssh_key_passphrase: foo
```


### Code of Conduct

- [X] I agree to follow the Ansible Code of Conduct

review_comments: This appears to be implemented for Alpine Linux only, this should be moved to the base class.
Are you sure? Line 1187 is in the base class (```class User(object)```). I'm relatively new to python so maybe I've overseen something.

I missed this earlier, this module uses several classes to create a 'per system' object to handle the actions, you only updated the class for Alpine (which is derived from busybox, which is derived from user).

We need to ensure that all variants get the update.

I've added an integration test called "test_ssh_key_rounds.yml". It creates an SSH key with 500 rounds. I'm not exactly sure but for me it looks like this test runs on all containers not only on Alpine.
